items.title: Graduate scheme applications
items.ask: An employer receives 15,000 applications. 60% are screened out after psychometric testing, a further 55% of the rest after an online interview, and 15% of those invited to assessment centres receive job offers. How many graduates received job offers? Options: 390, 395, 400, 405, 410.
items.how: 15,000 × 40% = 6,000 after psychometrics; 6,000 × 45% = 2,700 after the interview; 2,700 × 15% = 405 offers.

items.title: Cargo ship: total value (data sufficiency)
items.ask: Statement 1: the cargo ship makes 4 journeys from city B to city A and is 75% full each journey. Statement 2: each tonne of cargo is valued at $30,303.03. Note: a ship carries at most 275 tonnes. What is the total combined value of the cargo across all four trips?
items.answer: C. BOTH statements together are sufficient, but neither alone is.
items.how: Statement 1 gives the tonnes (4 × 275 × 75% = 825) and statement 2 gives the value per tonne, so 825 × $30,303.03 = about $25 million needs both.

items.title: George and the speed limit
items.ask: George drives at 30 metres per second. The speed limit is 70 miles per hour. By how much is he under or above the limit? (1 mile = 1.609344 km). Options: under by 6 mph, under by 3 mph, over by 3 mph, over by 6 mph, cannot say.
items.answer: B. Under by 3 miles per hour
items.vn: B. Under by 3 miles per hour

items.title: Who earns the most? (data sufficiency)
items.ask: Statement 1: Michelle and Janice’s combined income exceeds Albert’s. Statement 2: Michelle earns $5,000 per year more than Janice. Note: Albert earns double what Janice earns. Who earns the most of the three?
items.answer: E. Statements 1 and 2 together are NOT sufficient. (Not in the key’s notes: our working.)
items.how: Albert = 2J. Statement 1 only says Michelle > Janice. Statement 2 makes Michelle = J + 5,000, and she out-earns Albert only if J < 5,000, which is unknown. Statement 1 adds nothing once statement 2 is known.

items.title: Ralph’s profit
items.ask: Ralph sells his product for $9.99. He buys at the wholesale price of $39.50 for a pack of ten. How much profit does he make from the retail sale of 125 units? Options: $720.75, $725.25, $730.75, $735.25, $740.75.
items.how: 125 units need 13 packs of ten (12.5 rounds up): cost 13 × 39.50 = 513.50. Revenue 125 × 9.99 = 1,248.75. Profit = 735.25.

items.title: Antiviral research budget
items.ask: A pharmaceutical company spends 21% of its $75,000,000 annual budget on R&D. Half of this goes to antiviral drugs, and a quarter of antiviral research goes to improving existing drugs. How much is spent annually on improving existing antiviral drugs? Options: $1,756,750, $1,854,000, $1,968,750, $2,015,500, $2,157,250.
items.answer: C. $1,968,750 (Not in the key’s notes: our working.)

items.title: Phishing emails (data sufficiency)
items.ask: Statement 1: two thirds of all emails are legitimate from the contact list, 12.5% are advertisements, 15% are legitimate from senders not on the contact list; the remainder are phishing. Statement 2: on average 24 emails a day on weekdays and 11 a day at weekends. What is the probability that any given email is a phishing email?
items.answer: A. Statement 1 ALONE is sufficient. (Not in the key’s notes: our working.)
items.how: Phishing share = 1 − 2/3 − 12.5% − 15% = about 5.83%. Statement 2 only gives volumes, so it is not needed.

items.title: HR funding (data sufficiency)
items.ask: Statement 1: HR is the second lowest funded department. Statement 2: the lowest funded department was Customer Services (5%) and the third lowest was Finance (15%). Note: funding is allocated in 5% increments. How much funding will HR receive?
items.answer: C. BOTH statements together are sufficient, but neither alone is.
items.how: Statement 2 never says which department is second lowest. With statement 1 as well, HR sits between Customer Services (5%) and Finance (15%), so it gets 10%. The screenshot shows option B selected, but the key’s note gives C.

items.title: Art broker’s earnings
items.ask: An art broker earns a 10% commission on paintings sold. When auctioning, the broker earns an additional $150 per item through auction fees. If the broker sells 8 paintings not at auction for $8,000 each and 4 paintings at auction for $32,000 in total, how much does the broker earn? Options: $10,200, $11,400, $12,600, $13,800, $15,000.
items.vn: Thu từ not auction: 8,000 x 8 x 10% · Thu từ auction: 4 x 150 + 32,000 x 10% · Total: 10,200

items.title: GM crops: scientifically-controlled experiments
items.ask: Statement: There have been no experiments involving GM crops which have been carried out in a scientifically-controlled environment.
items.how: The passage says experiments to reassure the public about GM crops have been carried out under scientifically-controlled conditions.
items.vn: False (Dòng 4 từ dưới lên) — line 4 from the bottom

items.ask: Statement: Genetic change in plants could occur without the intervention of humans.
items.how: The passage says the genetic changes made by scientists ‘could in theory occur naturally’.

items.ask: Statement: Subsistence crops, if sold, will not generate a return on investment.
items.how: The passage says subsistence crops are grown to meet the needs of those producing them, but says nothing about what would happen if they were sold; the two ideas are not linked.

items.how: Nothing says cash crops cannot meet farmers’ needs. ‘Subsistence crops, unlike cash crops’ only concerns those producing them, not farmers in general.

items.title: GM crops: expected food shortages
items.ask: Statement: Some people expect global food shortages without the use of GM crops.
items.how: The passage says supporters expect GM crops could help alleviate food shortages. It does not say shortages are expected if GM crops are not used.
items.vn: Cannot say. Người ta mong đợi “food shortages sẽ giảm với GM crops”, không phải “food shortage sẽ xảy ra nếu KHÔNG có GM crops”

items.ask: Bar chart of product sales (£10,000s) by category for 2008 and 2009. In 2010 a High Street CD and DVDs sale raises the annual 2009 sales of each category by 11% and 14.5% respectively. What are the combined High Street DVD and CD sales for 2010? Options: £480,500, £514,118, £652,840, £0.56 million, £65.4 million.
items.answer: The key has no note for this item, and the screenshot is cropped so the DVD and CD bars cannot be read.
items.how: Apply +11% and +14.5% to the 2009 DVD and CD values on the full chart, then add them.

items.title: Trade balance: Japan’s imports in 2009
items.ask: 2008 trade balance chart and 2009 trade balance table (trade balance = exports − imports). If Japan’s exports value increased by 1/5th between 2008 and 2009, what was Japan’s imports value in 2009? Options: cannot say, $29,400 million, $23,560 million, $25,560 million, $29,440 million.
items.how: 2008 exports 29,400; × 1.2 = 35,280 in 2009; 2009 trade balance 5,840, so imports = 35,280 − 5,840 = $29,440 million. The screenshot already contains these steps.

items.title: UK trading vessels: gross tonnage per added vessel
items.ask: World fleet trading vessels table (2000–2008). Given the increase in UK trading vessels from 2006 to 2008, what was the average increase in Gross Tonnage (million) per added vessel? Options: 0.023, 0.028, 0.029, 0.032, 0.033.
items.answer: The key has no note for this item, and the screenshot shows only the gross tonnage table, not the number of vessels.
items.how: Increase in UK gross tonnage 2006 to 2008 (19.3 → 21.0 = 1.7) divided by the number of vessels added, which is on the part of the exhibit not shown.

items.title: Belgium’s average earnings
items.ask: If the ratio of France : Belgium average earnings per head of working population is 2:5, what is Belgium’s average earnings in £, at an exchange rate of 1.15 Euros to the £ (to the nearest £100)? France = 30,000. Options: £124,000, £86,000, £86,300, £124,800, £65,200.
items.answer: The notes and our working disagree. Notes: £86,300 (third option). Our working: £65,200 (last option). Please check against the real key.
items.how: Belgium = 30,000 ÷ 2 × 5 = 75,000. The notes multiply by 1.15 (86,250, rounded to 86,300). If 1.15 euros buy £1 and the table is in euros, the conversion divides: 75,000 ÷ 1.15 = £65,217, which rounds to £65,200.

items.title: Cake A: eggs to break even
items.ask: Cake recipes in grams with selling prices, and ingredient prices per kilogramme. How many grams of eggs would have to be added to Cake A so that it would not make a profit? Options: 60g, 65g, 125g, 160g, 240g.
items.how: Cake A costs 0.4 × 3 + 0.01 × 5 + 0.03 × 20 + 0.1 × 15 = 3.35. Not making a profit means cost = price 5.75, so 3.35 + 40x = 5.75 and x = 0.06 kg = 60 g.

items.title: China: urban population
items.ask: Urban population of China by year and China age structure 2017 (millions). If everyone aged 25–54 formed part of the urban population of China, how many people from the other age brackets would also live with them (millions)? Options: 143.71, 483.73, 674.25, 731.16.
items.how: Total population 1,405 million; urban at 58.2% = 817.71. Aged 25–54: 344 + 330 = 674. Remaining urban people from other ages: 817.71 − 674 = 143.71.
items.vn: Total china pop: 1405 · Urban pop: 1405*58.2% = 817.71 · Total 25-54 aged: 344 + 330 = 674 · Remain: 143.71

items.title: TV shows: total views with peak viewing
items.ask: If the TV shows received Peak Viewing for every episode of the series, how many more Total Views per Series (in millions) were there for Outsider compared with Pale Hills? Options: 0.6, 1.6, 3.2, 4.0 million and one more option below the screenshot.
items.how: Outsider: 8 episodes × 1.4 = 11.2. Pale Hills: 12 episodes × 0.8 = 9.6. Difference 1.6.

items.title: Books: physical sales
items.ask: Table of book sales by format with prices (physical £9.00, digital £6.50, audiobook £18.00). How much more money from physical sales did the least expensive book per page make compared to the most expensive book per page? Options: £13,599, £14,004, £15,447, £23,895, £27,720.
items.how: Per page, Lover’s Loss (808 pages) is cheapest and Jet Engines (222 pages) is dearest. Physical sales: 1,556 × £9 = £14,004 against 45 × £9 = £405, a difference of £13,599.

items.title: Advertising revenue: 2011 forecast
items.ask: Bar chart of advertising revenue 2006–2010 (£ billion) and a pie chart of the 2011 forecast. If the same absolute trends in advertising revenue from 2009 to 2010 continue for 2010 to 2011, what will be the 2011 advertising revenue for Television and Internet combined? Options: £8.1 billion, £16.2 billion, £21.2 billion, £12 billion, £10.6 billion.
items.answer: £12 billion (the fourth option, selected in the screenshot)
items.how: Internet 5.5 → 6.3 (+0.8) and Television 3.7 → 4.3 (+0.6). Continuing the same change: 7.1 + 4.9 = 12.0. The notes use the percentage trends (+14.55% and +16.2%), which give 7.22 + 5.00 = about 12.2, and also point to £12 billion.
items.vn: Trend internet 2009 – 2010: 14.55% · Trend television 2009 – 2010: 16.2% · Internet 2011 forecast: 6.3x(1+14.55%) · Television 2011 forecast: 4.3x(1+16.2%) · Total: 12
